title: cs-codex-turn reports a turn the provider ended with an error as a completed turn
foundBy: session agent operating two eight-member campaigns side by side on one host, reading every member's own CLI session records and the lender containers' logs after both campaigns had ended

evidence.verified: go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestCodexTurnReportsAProviderFailure -count=1: PASS, 4 cases. With the driver reverted, the same run fails all 4 with `exit = 0; want 5`. Three of the fixture events are what codex 0.152.1 wrote against a stub provider.

resolution: `cs-codex-turn` reads the `task_complete` event it waited for. When the event carries `error`, the driver exits 5, prints the provider's message on stderr, and prints `failure class=<class> retry_after=<secs>` for a caller to parse.
details:
**What happened.** Across two campaigns, 23 of 41 codex turns were ended by the provider: 21 on the key's tokens-per-minute limit and 2 on *"Selected model is at capacity"*. In the rollout JSONL each of those turns ends with a `task_complete` event whose `last_agent_message` is `null` and whose `error.message` carries the provider's text. The exit status of `cs-codex-turn` was 0 for every one of them.

**Why.** The driver's completion test is a count: it waits until the rollout holds more `task_complete` events than it did before the prompt was submitted, and then reports success. It never reads the event. Its documented exit codes are *0 ok, 2 turn timed out/stalled, 3 launch/setup failure, 1 usage*. There is no code for a turn that failed, so a caller cannot tell a model that finished from a provider that refused.

**The precedent is in the same directory.** `cs-opencode-turn` already treats this as its own case. Its header says provider-side API errors *"surface only on the session's"* record. It runs a post-check that is *"REQUIRED even on exit 0"*, and it exits **5, turn failed**. `cs-codex-turn` has no equivalent. Neither does `cs-claude-turn` (*0 ok, 2 turn timed out, 3 launch/setup failure, 1 usage/other*). It was not exercised by a provider error here, and it is named only because it has the same shape.

**What it costs downstream.** A campaign harness that sees a finished turn and no reply concludes the member stopped. It answers with a continue and then a restart, and each re-sends the member's whole context into the limit that ended the turn. Three healthy members were written off as stuck that way. That half is filed in the campaign ledger as SAC-034, and the missing reason as SAC-035. This record is the place the reason is first lost.

**How to reproduce.** Point `OPENAI_BASE_URL` at a stub that answers every model call with HTTP 429 and a rate-limit body, run one prompt through `cs-codex-turn`, and wait out codex's retries. Expected today: exit status 0, with the rollout's last `task_complete` carrying an `error`. Described from the observed records and from reading the driver; not yet run against a stub.

**What would fix it.** Read the `task_complete` event the driver was waiting for. If it carries an `error`, exit with a failed-turn code as `cs-opencode-turn` does, and print the provider's message on stderr. Better still, classify it (throttled, at capacity, unauthorized, context too long, other) on a line a caller can parse. Include the provider's retry-after when it gives one.

notes.text: The `details` text was copy-edited so the repository's prose gate passes: long sentences were split and em-dashes removed, and no claim was changed. The text as filed is in commit c059533.

The failure was reproduced with codex 0.152.1 against a stub provider. A refused turn ends with `task_complete` carrying `error.message` and `error.codex_error_info`, as the record describes. The second field is codex's own classification, and the driver reads it before it falls back on the message.

The fix differs from what was asked in two places. The record asks for the provider's retry-after. Codex does not write that header to the rollout, so `retry_after` is parsed from the provider's message, and it is `-` when the message names no wait. `cs-claude-turn` was left alone, because no failed claude turn has been observed to take the shape from. SBX-051 holds that half.
A failed turn still prints the session id. The TUI outlives the failure, so the caller can send the prompt again to the same session and does not need a restart.

The driver has now been run against a real codex TUI in a sandbox, with a rate limit injected by `cs-sandbox lender fault`. It exited 5 after 32 seconds with `failure class=throttled retry_after=2`, and it printed the session id. A second turn sent to that session with `--uuid` met a throttle that cleared, exited 0 with the answer, and left one session file.
